passages.text: The righteous live a life of integrity; happy are their children after them.
The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life, and he who is wise wins souls.
The name of Adonai is a strong tower; a righteous person runs to it and is raised high [above danger].
Acting justly is a joy for the righteous but it terrifies evildoers.
A wise man can go up into a city of warriors and undermine the strength in which it trusts.
With his mouth the hypocrite can ruin his neighbor, but by knowledge the righteous are delivered.
The righteousness of the upright rescues them, but the treacherous are trapped by their own intrigues.
Don’t lurk like an outlaw near the home of the righteous, don’t raid the place where he lives.
The teaching of a wise man is a fountain of life, enabling one to avoid deadly traps.
Adonai does not let the righteous go hungry, but he thwarts the craving of the wicked.
Blessings are for the head of the righteous, but the speech of the wicked is a cover for violence.
The memory of the righteous will be for a blessing, but the reputation of the wicked will rot.
Wise-hearted people take orders, but a babbling fool will have trouble.
The righteous is delivered from trouble, and the wicked comes to take his place.
When the righteous prosper, the city rejoices; and when the wicked perish, there is joy.
A righteous man takes care of his animal, but the wicked? Even his compassion is cruel.
A righteous person hates lying, but the wicked is vile and disgraceful.
Adonai detests the sacrifices of the wicked but delights in the prayers of the upright.
Like a muddied spring or a polluted well is a righteous person who gives way before the wicked.
In an evil person’s crime is a trap, but the righteous sing and rejoice.
The righteous person eats his fill, but the belly of the wicked is empty.
The wicked flee when no one pursues them; but the righteous, like lions, feel sure of themselves.
When the wicked rise up, people hide; but when they perish, the righteous flourish.
If the righteous are paid what they deserve here on earth, how much more the wicked and the sinner!
The Righteous One observes the house of the wicked; he overthrows the wicked to their ruin.
By the blessing of the upright, a city is raised up; but the words of the wicked tear it down.
A wise person fears and turns away from evil, but a fool is reckless and overconfident.
The plans of the righteous are just, but the schemes of the wicked are deceitful.
A backslider is filled up with his own ways, but a good person gets satisfaction from himself.
The righteous guides his friend’s way rightly, but the way of the wicked will lead them astray.
The proverbs of Shlomo: A wise son is a joy to his father, but a foolish son is a grief to his mother.
The heart’s real intentions are like deep water; but a person with discernment draws them out.
The wealth of the rich is his fortified city, like a high wall, in his own imagination.
No good comes from ill-gotten wealth, but righteousness rescues from death.
The righteousness of the innocent levels their way, but wickedness of the wicked makes them fall.
When a wicked man dies, his hope perishes; what he hopes for from evil comes to nothing.
Righteousness protects him whose way is honest, but wickedness brings down the sinner.
Adonai detests the way of the wicked but loves anyone who pursues righteousness.
When a man’s ways please Adonai, he makes even the man’s enemies be at peace with him.
The words of a man’s mouth are deep water, a gushing torrent, a fountain of wisdom.
He who pursues righteousness and kindness finds life, prosperity and honor.
The clever see trouble coming and hide; the simple go on and pay the penalty.
The profits of the wicked are illusory; but those who sow righteousness gain a true reward.
Genuine righteousness leads to life, but the pursuer of evil goes to his own death.
For though he falls seven times, he will get up again; it’s the wicked who fail under stress.

Better open rebuke than hidden love.

Wounds from a friend are received as well-meant, but an enemy’s kisses are insincere.
The clever see trouble coming and hide; the thoughtless go on and pay the penalty.
When the just are triumphant, there is great rejoicing, but when the wicked rise up, people hide.
A wicked messenger falls into evil, but a faithful envoy brings healing.
The evil plans of the foolish are sin, and people detest a scorner.
For the evil person has no future — the lamp of the wicked will go out.
Rather meet a bear robbed of its cubs than encounter a fool in his folly.
When a wicked person comes, contempt comes too, and with disdain, provocation.
The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination; how much more when he brings it with vile motives.
Don’t get upset because of evildoers; don’t be envious of the wicked.
Telling a message to a fool and sending him out is like cutting off one’s feet and drinking violence.
Like one who ties his stone to the sling is he who gives honor to a fool.
A master can make anything, but hiring a fool is like hiring some passer-by.
You can crush a fool in a mortar with a pestle, along with the grain being crushed; yet his foolishness will not leave him.
A violent man lures his neighbor astray and leads him into evil ways.
He who plans to do evil people call a schemer.
Like snow in summer or rain at harvest-time, so honor for a fool is out of place.
Don’t answer a fool in terms of his folly, or you will be descending to his level;
Once the wicked are down, it’s the end of them; but the house of the upright endures.
Keep clear of a fool, for you won’t hear a sensible word from him.
A wicked man puts on a bold face, whereas the upright prepares his ways.
The legs of the disabled hang limp and useless; likewise a proverb in the mouth of a fool.
Just as a dog returns to his vomit, a fool repeats his folly.
Do you see someone who thinks himself wise? There is more hope for a fool than for him!
Stone is heavy and sand a dead weight, but a fool’s provocation outweighs them both.
An evil person seeks only rebellion, but a cruel messenger will be sent against him.
Like a thorn branch in the hand of a drunk is a proverb in the mouth of a fool.
Those who trouble their families inherit the wind, and the fool becomes slave to the wise.
The wicked are brought down by their wrongdoing, but the righteous can be confident even at death.
but answer a fool as his folly deserves, so that he won’t think he is wise.
When the wicked flourish, wrongdoing flourishes; but the righteous will witness their downfall.
Don’t envy sinners, but follow the example of those who always fear God;
The wicked serve as a ransom for the righteous, and likewise the perfidious for the upright.
Whoever causes the honest to pursue evil ways will himself fall into his own pit, but the pure-hearted will inherit good.
The wisdom of the cautious makes him know where he is going, but the folly of fools misleads them.
Guilt offerings make a mockery of fools; but among the upright there is good will.
Common sense is a fountain of life to one who has it, whereas fools are punished by their own folly.
One who winks knowingly is planning deceit; one who pinches his lips together has already done wrong.
He who separates himself indulges his desires and shows contempt for sound advice of any kind.
The person who strays from the way of common sense will come to rest in the company of the dead.
Thorns and snares beset the way of the stubborn; he who values his life keeps his distance from them.
The mouth of an adulteress is a deep pit; the man with whom Adonai is angry falls into it.
for then you will have a future; what you hope for will not be cut off.
Relying on an untrustworthy person in a time of trouble is like [relying on] a broken tooth or an unsteady leg.
Men of blood hate those who are pure and seek the life of the upright.
Grace and truth preserve a king; with grace he upholds his throne.
A king’s glory lies in having many subjects; if the prince’s people are few, it is his ruin.
The king seated on his judgment throne can winnow out all evil with his glance.
It is an abomination for a king to do evil, for the throne is made secure by righteousness.
Remove the wicked from the king’s presence, and his throne will rest firmly on righteousness.
If a king steadfastly gives justice to the poor, his throne will be secure forever.
When the king’s face brightens, it means life; his favor is like the clouds that bring spring rain.
The dread of a king is like when a lion roars; he who makes him angry commits a life-threatening sin.
These also are proverbs of Shlomo; the men of Hizkiyah king of Y’hudah copied them out:
Don’t put yourself forward in the king’s presence; don’t take a place among the great.
If a ruler listens to lies, all his officials will be wicked.
A prince without discernment is a cruel oppressor, but one who hates greed will prolong his life.
A king’s wrath is like the roaring of a lion, but his favor is like dew on the grass.
He who loves the pure-hearted and is gracious in speech will have the king as his friend.
A king shows favor to a servant with good sense, but his wrath strikes one who shames [him].
The king’s heart in Adonai’s hand is like streams of water — he directs it wherever he pleases.
A king gives stability to a country by justice, but one who overtaxes it brings it to ruin.
Like a roaring lion or a bear prowling for food is a wicked ruler over a poor people.
The king’s anger is a herald of death, and one who is wise will appease it.
Divine inspiration is on the lips of the king, so his mouth must be faithful when he judges.
For it is better to be told, “Come up here,” than be degraded in the presence of a nobleman. What your eyes have seen,
A wise king winnows the wicked [from the righteous] and threshes them under the cartwheel.
The king should delight in righteous lips, and he should love someone who speaks what is right.
The evil bow down before the good, and the wicked at the gates of the righteous.
Righteousness makes a nation great, but sin degrades any people.
The balance and scales of justice have their origin in Adonai; all the weights in the bag are his doing.
An intelligent slave will rule a shameful son and share the inheritance with the brothers.
God gets glory from concealing things; kings get glory from investigating things.
Like the sky for height or the earth for depth is the heart of kings — unfathomable.
Remove the impurities from the silver, and the smith has material to make a vessel.
A whip for a horse, a bridle for a donkey, and a rod for the back of fools.
A land which transgresses [is punished by] having many rulers; but with a man of understanding and knowledge, stability is prolonged.
When the righteous flourish, the people rejoice; but when the wicked are in power, the people groan.
The righteous understands the cause of the poor, but the wicked is unconcerned.
The human spirit is a lamp of Adonai; it searches one’s inmost being.
Hope deferred makes the heart sick, but desire fulfilled is a tree of life.
The heart knows its own bitterness, and no stranger can share its joy.
Even in laughter the heart can be sad, and joy may end in sorrow.
A glad heart makes a face happy, but heartache breaks the spirit.
A cheerful glance brings joy to the heart, and good news invigorates the bones.
A happy heart is good medicine, but low spirits sap one’s strength.
Like removing clothes on a chilly day or like vinegar on soda is someone who sings songs to a heavy heart.
Desire fulfilled is sweet to the soul, but turning away from evil is abhorrent to fools.
The hearing ear and the seeing eye — Adonai made them both.
If you have a big appetite, put a knife to your throat!
Who has misery? Who has regret? Who fights and complains all the time? Who gets bruised for no good reason? Who has bloodshot eyes?
Your eyes will see peculiar things, your mind will utter nonsense.
Just as water reflects the face, so one human heart reflects another.
A man’s lust is his shame, and a poor man is better than a liar.
If you make your eyes rush at it, it’s no longer there! For wealth will surely grow wings, like an eagle flying off to the sky.
Wine is a mocker, strong liquor a rowdy; anyone led astray by it is unwise.
A bribe works like a charm, in the view of him who gives it — wherever it turns, it succeeds.
A person’s spirit can sustain him when ill, but a crushed spirit — who can bear it?
A person’s gift clears his way and gives him access to the great.
To act without knowing how you function is not good; and if you rush ahead, you will miss your goal.
The pride of the young is their strength; the dignity of the old is gray hair.
When you sit down to dine with a ruler, think carefully about who is before you.
Don’t be greedy for his delicacies, for they are deceptive food.
Don’t exhaust yourself in pursuit of wealth; be smart enough to desist.
Don’t eat the food of a stingy man; don’t be greedy for his delicacies.
For he is like someone who keeps accounts — “Eat! Drink!” he says to you, but he doesn’t really mean it.
The little you eat you will vomit up, and your compliments will have been wasted.
Don’t be one of those who guzzle wine or of those who eat meat to excess,
for both drunkard and glutton will become poor — drowsiness will clothe them with rags.
Those who spend their time over wine, those always trying out mixed drinks.
Don’t gaze at the red wine as it gives its color to the cup. It may glide down smoothly now;
but in the end, it bites like a serpent — yes, it strikes like a poisonous snake.

You will feel as if lying on the waves of the sea or sprawled on top of the mast — “They hit me, but I didn’t feel it! They beat me up, and I didn’t even know it! When will I wake up? . . . I’ll go get another drink.”
If you find honey, eat only what you need; for if you eat too much of it, you may throw it up;
so don’t visit your neighbor too much, or he may get his fill of you and come to hate you.
A person who is full loathes a honeycomb; but to the hungry, any bitter thing is sweet.
Like a bird that strays from its nest is a man who strays from his home.
The proud will be humbled, but the humble will be honored.
First comes pride, then disgrace; but with the humble is wisdom.
Better to be humble among the poor than share the spoil with the proud.
Before being ruined, a person’s heart is proud; before being honored, a person must be humble.
Haughty looks, a proud heart — what the wicked plow is sin.
Adonai will pull down the houses of the proud, but preserves intact the widow’s boundaries.
Adonai detests all those with proud hearts; be assured that they will not go unpunished.
Pride goes before destruction, and arrogance before failure.
Don’t boast about tomorrow, for you don’t know what the day may bring.
“Scoffer” is what you call a proud, insolent person who acts with overweening conceit.
It isn’t good to eat too much honey or to seek honor after honor.
The reward for humility is fear of Adonai, along with wealth, honor and life.
It is harder to win an offended brother than a strong city; their fights are like the bars of a fortress.
A person wins praise in keeping with his common sense, but a person with a warped mind is treated with contempt.
A person with upright conduct fears Adonai, but a person who is devious scorns him.
All a man’s ways are pure in his own view, but Adonai weighs the spirit.
The crucible [tests] silver, and the furnace [tests] gold, but the one who tests hearts is Adonai.
Starting a fight is like letting water through [a dike] — better stop the quarrel before it gets worse.
All a person’s ways are right in his own view, but Adonai weighs the heart.
The wicked is set on evil; he doesn’t pity even his neighbor.
Don’t be envious of evil people, and don’t desire to be with them.
For their minds are occupied with violence, and their lips speak of making trouble.
Let someone else praise you, not your own mouth, a stranger and not your own lips.
The crucible [tests] silver, and the furnace [tests] gold, but a person [is tested] by [his reaction to] praise.
Happy the person who is never without fear, but he who hardens his heart will fall into misfortune.
People with good sense are slow to anger, and it is their glory to overlook an offense.
Angry people stir up strife; hot-tempered people commit many crimes.
Hot-tempered people stir up strife, but patient people quiet quarrels.
Being slow to anger goes with great understanding, being quick-tempered makes folly still worse.
Avoiding quarrels brings a person honor; for any fool can explode in anger.
Fury is cruel and anger overwhelming, but who can stand up to jealousy?
Don’t associate with an angry man; make no hot-tempered man your companion.

If there’s no wood, the fire goes out; if nobody gossips, contention stops.

As coals are to embers and wood to fire is a quarrelsome person to kindling strife.
A secret gift allays anger, and a bribe under the cloak the strongest fury.
He who is quick-tempered does stupid things, and one who does vile things is hated.
Like someone who grabs a dog by the ears is a passer-by who mixes in a fight not his own.
Those who love quarreling love giving offense; those who make their gates tall are courting disaster.
A violent-tempered person will be punished; if you try to save him from it, you make things worse.
Hate stirs up disputes, but love covers all kinds of transgressions.
A tranquil mind gives health to the body, but envy rots the bones.
He who conceals an offense promotes love, but he who harps on it can separate even close friends.
If you do, you may learn his ways and find yourself caught in a trap.
With patience a ruler may be won over, and a gentle tongue can break bones.
Scoffers can inflame a city, but the wise can calm the fury.

themes.name: Man and Woman Family and Friends

passages.text: Whoever curses his father or mother — his lamp will go out in total darkness.
So let your father and mother be glad; let her who gave you birth rejoice.
One who mistreats his father and evicts his mother is a son who brings them shame and disgrace.
A capable wife is a crown for her husband, but a shameful one is like rot in his bones.
It is better to live on a corner of the roof than to share the house with a nagging wife.
It is better to live in the desert than with a nagging, irritable wife.
It is better to live on a corner of the roof than to share the house with a nagging wife.
Listen to your father, who gave you life; and don’t despise your mother when she gets old.
A son who is a fool is his father’s ruin, and a nagging wife is like a leak that keeps dripping.

Perfume and incense make the heart glad, [also] friendship sweet with advice from the heart.

Don’t abandon a friend who is also a friend of your father. Don’t enter your brother’s house on the day of your calamity — better a neighbor nearby than a brother far away.
A wise son observes Torah, but a friend of those lacking restraint shames his father.

A leak that keeps dripping on a rainy day and the nagging of a wife are the same —

whoever can restrain her can restrain the wind or keep perfume on his hand from making itself known.
A righteous person’s father will be filled with joy; yes, he whose son is wise will rejoice in him.
A friend shows his friendship at all times — it is for adversity that [such] a brother is born.
He who finds a wife finds a great good; he has won the favor of Adonai.
Some “friends” pretend to be friends, but a true friend sticks closer than a brother.
Just as iron sharpens iron, a person sharpens the character of his friend.
Every wise woman builds up her home, but a foolish one tears it down with her own hands.
A house and wealth are inherited from ancestors, but a sensible wife is from Adonai.
My son, give me your heart; let your eyes observe my ways.
A gracious woman obtains honor; aggressive men obtain wealth.
Like a gold ring in the snout of a pig is a beautiful woman who lacks good sense.
White hair is a crown of honor obtained by righteous living.
Grandchildren are the crown of the aged, while the glory of children is their ancestors.
The character of even a child is known by how he acts, by whether his deeds are pure and right.
Train a child in the way he [should] go; and, even when old, he will not swerve from it.
Whoever robs mother or father and says, “That’s not a crime!” is comrade to the destroyer.
A prostitute is a deep ditch, and a forbidden woman like a narrow well.
She lies in wait to snatch her prey and adds to the number of faithless men.
The fear of Adonai leads to life; one who has it is satisfied and rests untouched by evil.
For the prudent, the path of life goes upward; thus he avoids Sh’ol below.
Good common sense produces grace, but the way of the treacherous is rough.
He who walks purely walks securely, but he who walks in crooked ways will be found out.
A person may plan his path, but Adonai directs his steps.
The fear of Adonai adds length to life, but the years of the wicked are cut short.
He who observes discipline is on the way to life; but he who ignores correction is making a mistake.
In the road of righteousness is life; no death is in its pathway.
No one is made secure by wickedness, but the roots of the righteous will never be moved.
What the righteous hope for will end in joy; what the wicked expect will come to nothing.
The way of Adonai is a stronghold to the upright but ruin to those who do evil.
The righteous will never be moved, but the wicked will not remain in the land.
To a fool, vileness is like a game, as is wisdom to a person of discernment.
What a fool dreads will overtake him, but the righteous will be given his desire.
When the storm has passed, the wicked are gone; but the righteous are firmly established forever.
The integrity of the upright guides them, but the duplicity of the treacherous destroys them.
A man who is kind does himself good, but the cruel does harm to himself.
The righteous desire only good, but what the wicked hope for brings wrath.
He who strives for good obtains favor, but he who searches for evil — it comes to him!
Deceit is in the hearts of those who plot evil, but for those advising peace there is joy.
No harm can come to the righteous, but the wicked are overwhelmed with disaster.
The light of the righteous [shines] joyfully, but the lamp of the wicked will be extinguished.
He who walks with the wise will become wise, but the companion of fools will suffer.
There can be a way which seems right to a person, but at its end are the ways of death.
One who doesn’t think believes every word, but the cautious understands his steps.
Won’t those who plot evil go astray? But grace and truth are for those who plan good.
Discipline is severe for one who leaves the way, and whoever can’t stand correction will die.
Folly appeals to one who lacks sense, but a person of discernment goes straight ahead.
Grace and truth atone for iniquity, and people turn from evil through fear of Adonai.
Avoiding evil is the highway of the upright; he who watches his step preserves his life.
There can be a way which seems right to a person, but at its end are the ways of death.
One can cast lots into one’s lap, but the decision comes from Adonai.
A person’s own folly is what ruins his way, but he rages in his heart against Adonai.
He who keeps a mitzvah keeps himself safe, but he who doesn’t care how he lives will die.
One can devise many plans in one’s mind, but Adonai’s plan will prevail.
Most people announce that they show kindness, but who can find someone faithful [enough to do it]?
A man’s steps are ordered by Adonai, so how can a person understand his own ways?
A horse may be prepared for the day of battle, but victory comes from Adonai.
You, my son: listen, be wise, and set your mind on the right way.
He who conceals his sins will not succeed; he who confesses and abandons them will gain mercy.
Whoever lives blamelessly will be saved, but he whose ways are crooked will fall in one [of those ways].
Fearing human beings is a snare; but he who trusts in Adonai will be raised high [above danger].
The fear of Adonai is the beginning of knowledge, but fools despise wisdom and discipline.
The discipline of wisdom is fear of Adonai, so before being honored, a person must be humble.
A scoffer seeks wisdom in vain, but knowledge comes easily to someone with discernment.
In the fear of Adonai is powerful security; for his children there will be a place of refuge.
He who spurns discipline detests himself, but he who listens to correction grows in understanding.
The fear of Adonai is a fountain of life enabling one to avoid deadly traps.
How much better than gold it is to gain wisdom! Yes, rather than money, choose to gain understanding.
Know that wisdom is similar[ly sweet] to your soul; if you find it, then you will have a future, what you hope for will not be cut off.
I have written you worthwhile things full of good counsel and knowledge,
Why would a fool wish to pay for wisdom when he has no desire to learn?
Insolence produces only strife, but wisdom is found with those who take advice.
Wisdom is at rest in a person with discernment, but in fools it has to call attention to itself.
No wisdom, discernment or counsel succeeds against Adonai.
The mind of a person with discernment gets knowledge, and the ear of the wise seeks knowledge.
A rebuke makes more impression on a person of understanding than a hundred blows on a fool.
Thoughtless people inherit folly, but the cautious are crowned with knowledge.
Pay attention, and listen to the words of the wise; apply your heart to my knowledge;
The mind of a person with discernment seeks knowledge, but the mouth of a fool feeds on folly.
A wise man is strong; yes, a man of knowledge grows in strength.
Discipline your child while there is hope, but don’t get so angry that you kill him!
He who trusts in himself is a fool, but he who lives by wisdom will escape.
The eyes of Adonai protect [the man with] knowledge, but he overturns the plans of a traitor.
Every cautious person acts with knowledge, but a fool parades his folly.
If you strike a scorner, the simple will learn to act wisely; if you reprove the intelligent, he will understand what you mean.
Whoever loves wisdom brings joy to his father, but a patron of prostitutes wastes his wealth.
The discerning person focuses on wisdom there before him, but a fool’s eyes wander to the ends of the earth.
Doing wrong is firmly tied to the heart of a child, but the rod of discipline will drive it far away from him.
When a scorner is punished, the simple become wiser; and when the wise is instructed, he takes hold of knowledge.
A person may have gold and a wealth of pearls, but lips informed by knowledge are a precious jewel.
He who heeds life-giving correction will be at home in the company of the wise.
A wise-hearted person is said to have discernment, and sweetness of speech adds to learning.
For with clever strategy you wage your war, and victory comes from having many advisers.
He who despises a word will suffer for it, but he who respects a command will be rewarded.
If you entrust all you do to Adonai, your plans will achieve success.
for it is pleasant to keep them deep within you; have all of them ready on your lips.
I want your trust to be in Adonai; this is why I’m instructing you about them today.
so you will know that these sayings are certainly true and bring back true sayings to him who sent you.
The proverbs of Shlomo: A wise son is a joy to his father, but a foolish son is a grief to his mother.
Without clever tactics an army is defeated, and victory comes from much planning.
Fools suppose their way is straight, but the wise pay attention to advice.
Poverty and shame are for him who won’t be taught, but he who heeds reproof will be honored.
A scorner does not like being corrected; he won’t go to the wise [for advice].
A wise son is a joy to his father, and only a fool despises his mother.
Without deliberation, plans go wrong; but with many advisers, they succeed.
He who controls his temper is better than a war hero, he who rules his spirit better than he who captures a city.
He who fathers a fool does so to his sorrow, and the father of a boor has no joy.
A son who is a fool means anger for his father and bitterness for the mother who gave him birth.
To acquire good sense is to love oneself; to treasure discernment is to prosper.
After consultation, plans succeed; so take wise advice when waging war.
Blows that wound purge away evil, yes, beatings [cleanse] one’s inmost being.
My son, if your heart is wise, then my own heart too is glad;
my inmost being rejoices when your lips say what is right.
My son, eat honey, for it is good; honeycomb drippings are sweet to your taste.
My son, become wise, and gladden my heart, so that I can answer my critics.
The rich man is wise in his own view, but the poor who has discernment sees through him.
Without a prophetic vision, the people throw off all restraint; but he who keeps Torah is happy.
“How happy the person whom God corrects! So don’t despise Shaddai’s discipline.

Also you have forgotten the counsel which speaks with you as sons: “My son, don’t despise the discipline of Adonai or become despondent when he corrects you. For Adonai disciplines those he loves and whips everyone he accepts as a son.”
As for me, I rebuke and discipline everyone I love; so exert yourselves, and turn from your sins!

For they disciplined us only for a short time and only as best they could; but he disciplines us in a way that provides genuine benefit to us and enables us to share in his holiness. Now, all discipline, while it is happening, does indeed seem painful, not enjoyable; but for those who have been trained by it, it later produces its peaceful fruit, which is righteousness.
Discipline is severe for one who leaves the way, and whoever can’t stand correction will die.
He who spurns discipline detests himself, but he who listens to correction grows in understanding.
The rod and rebuke give wisdom, but a child left to himself brings shame on his mother.
A son who heeds his father’s discipline is wise, but a scoffer doesn’t listen to rebuke.
Listen to advice, and accept discipline, so that in the end you will be wise.
He who loves knowledge loves discipline, but he who hates correction is a boor.
Therefore, say to them, ‘This is the nation that has not listened to the voice of Adonai their God. They won’t take correction; faithfulness has perished; it has vanished from their mouths.
How happy the man whom you correct, Yah, whom you teach from your Torah,
He who heeds life-giving correction will be at home in the company of the wise.
He who remains stiffnecked after much rebuke will be suddenly and incurably broken.
Adonai, your eyes look for truth. You struck them, but they weren’t affected; you [nearly] destroyed them, but they refused correction. They made their faces harder than rock, refusing to repent.
My son, if you stop heeding discipline, you will stray from the principles of knowledge.
A fool despises his father’s discipline, but he who heeds warnings is prudent.
Don’t withhold discipline from a child — if you beat him with a stick, he won’t die!
For the mitzvah is a lamp, Torah is light, and reproofs that discipline are the way to life.
He who fails to use a stick hates his son, but he who loves him is careful to discipline him.
Discipline your son, and he will give you rest; yes, he will be your delight.
Buy the truth, don’t sell it, also wisdom, discipline and discernment.
Apply your mind to discipline and your ears to words of knowledge.
The discipline of wisdom is fear of Adonai, so before being honored, a person must be humble.
But when we are judged by the Lord, we are being disciplined, so that we will not be condemned along with the world.
Yah disciplined me severely, but did not hand me over to death.
If you beat him with a stick, you will save him from Sh’ol.
Like a city breached, without walls, is a person who lacks self-control.
A slave can’t be disciplined with words; he may understand, but he won’t respond.
A slave who is pampered from youth will in the end be ungrateful.
The diligent will rule, while the lazy will be put to forced labor.
A lazy person won’t plow in winter; so at harvest-time, when he looks, there is nothing.
The lazy person wants but doesn’t have; the diligent get their desires filled.
A lazy man’s craving will kill him, because his hands refuse to work — he covets greedily all day long; but a righteous person gives without holding back.
A lazy man doesn’t roast what he hunted; but when a man is diligent, his wealth is precious.
Idle hands bring poverty; diligent hands bring wealth.
Whoever is lazy in doing his work is brother to the destroyer.
Laziness makes people fall asleep, and an idle person will go hungry.
The plans of the diligent lead only to abundance; but all who rush in arrive only at want.
A lazy man says, “There’s a lion outside! I’ll be killed if I go out in the street!”
Do you see a man skilled at his work? He will serve kings, not obscure people.
I passed by the field of the lazy man and the vineyard of the man lacking sense.
The lazy person says, “There’s a lion in the streets! A lion is roaming loose out there!” The door turns on its hinges, and the lazy man on his bed.
A sensible person gathers in summer, but he who sleeps during harvest is an embarrassment.
He who farms his land will have plenty of food, but he who follows futilities has no sense.
The lazy person buries his hand in the dish but doesn’t even bother to bring it to his mouth.
The lazy person buries his hand in the dish but is too tired to return it to his mouth.
Prepare your outside work, and get things ready for yourself on the land; after that, build your house.
Like vinegar to the teeth and smoke to the eyes is a lazy person to his employer.
A lazy man is wiser in his own view than seven who can answer with sense.
The lazy person’s way seems overgrown by thorns, but the path of the upright is a level highway.
He who farms his land will have plenty of food, but he who follows futilities will have plenty of poverty.
In all work there is profit, but mere talk produces only poverty.
A criminal’s conduct is crooked, but the work of the pure is right.
He who has skill in a matter will succeed; he who trusts in Adonai will be happy.
Where there are no oxen, the stalls are clean; but much is produced by the strength of an ox.
“I’ll just lie here a bit, rest a little longer, just fold my hands for a little more sleep” — and poverty comes marching in on you, scarcity hits you like an invading soldier.
The activity of the righteous is for life; the income of the wicked is for sin.
The crown of the wise is their riches, but the folly of fools is just that — folly.
If you love sleep, you will become poor; keep your eyes open, and you’ll have plenty of food.
Food obtained by fraud may taste good, but later the mouth is full of gravel.
No good comes from ill-gotten wealth, but righteousness rescues from death.
Adonai does not let the righteous go hungry, but he thwarts the craving of the wicked.
He who guarantees a loan for a stranger will suffer, but refusing to underwrite is safe.
A working man’s appetite acts on his behalf, because his hunger presses him on.
“Really bad stuff!” says the buyer [to the seller]; then he goes off and brags [about his bargain].
Possessions acquired quickly at first will not be blessed in the end.
There it was, overgrown with thistles; the ground was covered with nettles, and its stone wall was broken down.
I looked, and I thought about it; I saw, and I learned this lesson:
Whoever tends the fig tree will eat its fruit, and he who is attentive to his master will be honored.

Take care to know the condition of your flocks, and pay attention to your herds.

For wealth doesn’t last forever, neither does a crown through all generations.

When the hay has been mown, and the new grass appears, and the mountain greens have been gathered;

the lambs will provide your clothing, the goats will sell for enough to buy a field,

and there will be enough goat’s milk to [buy] food for you and your household and maintenance for your servant-girls.
There are those with nothing who pretend they are rich, also those with great wealth who pretend they are poor.
Rather than wealth, choose a good reputation, esteem over silver and gold.
The rich rule the poor, and the borrower is slave to the lender.
The rich man may have to ransom his life, but a poor man gets no threats.
Rich and poor have this in common — Adonai made them both.
Better to be poor and live an honest life than be crooked in one’s ways, though rich.
He who increases his wealth by charging exorbitant interest amasses it for someone who will bestow it on the poor.
The wealth of the rich is his fortified city; the ruin of the poor is their poverty.
The poor are disliked even by their peers, but the rich have many friends.
Wealth brings in many friends, but the poor man loses the one friend he has.
The blessing of Adonai is what makes people rich, and he doesn’t mix sorrow with it.
For the poor, every day is hard; but the good-hearted have a perpetual feast.
Pleasure-lovers will suffer want; he who loves wine and oil won’t get rich.
He who is generous is blessed, because he shares his food with the poor.
A trustworthy person will receive many blessings, but one rushing to get rich will not go unpunished.
A good man leaves an inheritance to his grandchildren, but the wealth of a sinner is stored up for the righteous.
Wealth gotten by worthless means dwindles away, but he who amasses it by hard work will increase it.
He who gives to the poor will lack nothing, but he who hides his eyes will get curses in plenty.
Better little with the fear of Adonai than great wealth coupled with worry.
Better to be poor and live one’s life uprightly than engage in crooked speech, for such a one is a fool.
A poor man’s relatives all hate him; even more his friends stay away from him. He may pursue them with entreaties, but they aren’t there to be found.
On the day of wrath, wealth doesn’t help; but righteousness rescues from death.
The home of the righteous is a storehouse of treasure, but the earnings of the wicked bring trouble.
In the home of the wise are fine treasures and oil, but a fool quickly devours it.
and by knowledge its rooms are filled with all kinds of costly and pleasant possessions.
It isn’t fitting for a fool to live in luxury, and even less for a slave to govern princes.
Better a little with righteousness than a huge income with injustice.
Some give freely and still get richer, while others are stingy but grow still poorer.
The person who blesses others will prosper; he who satisfies others will be satisfied himself.
The people will curse him who withholds grain; but if he sells it, blessings will be on his head.
He who trusts in his riches will fall, but the righteous will flourish like sprouting leaves.
A good man obtains Adonai’s favor, but the schemer his condemnation.
Better to be despised and have a servant than to boast of one’s status but have nothing to eat.
The wicked covet the loot of evil men, but the root of the righteous gives forth of itself.
Evil pursues sinners, but prosperity will reward the righteous.
The house of the wicked will be destroyed, but the tent of the upright will flourish.
Better a vegetable dinner with love than a stall-fattened ox with hate.
Better a dry piece of bread with calm than a house full of food but also full of strife.
He who gives his hand to guarantee a loan for his neighbor lacks good sense.
Seize his clothes, because he guaranteed a stranger’s loan; take them as security for that unknown woman.
A fortune gained by a lying tongue is vapor dispersed [by] seekers of death.
Don’t be one of those who give pledges, guaranteeing loans made to others;
for if you don’t have the wherewithal to pay, they will take your bed away from underneath you.
By wisdom a house is built, by understanding it is made secure,
Seize his clothes because he guaranteed a stranger’s loan; take them as security for that unknown woman.
He who is greedy rushes after riches, not knowing that want will overtake him.
A grasping disposition stirs up strife, but he who trusts in Adonai will prosper.
A person’s belly will be filled with the fruit of his mouth; with what his lips produce he will be filled.
Whoever guards his mouth and tongue keeps himself out of trouble.
A lying tongue hates its victims, and a flattering mouth causes ruin.
A worthless person digs up evil [gossip] — it is like scorching fire on his lips.
A slanderer’s words are tasty morsels; they slide right down into the belly.
A fool’s words get him into fights; yes, his mouth calls out for a beating.
He who covers up hate has lips that lie, and anyone who slanders is a fool.
A slanderer’s words are tasty morsels; they slide right down into the belly.
A person is responsible to prepare his heart, but how the tongue speaks is from Adonai.
Don’t speak in the ears of a fool, for he will only despise the common sense in your words.
A gossip goes around revealing secrets, so don’t get involved with a talkative person.
The lips of the righteous know what is wanted, but the mouth of the wicked [knows] deceit.
A fool’s mouth is his ruin; his words are a trap for him.
The mouth of the righteous brings forth wisdom, but the perverse tongue will be cut off.
From the mouth of a fool sprouts pride, but the lips of the wise protect them.
The wise man’s heart teaches his mouth, and to his lips it adds learning.
Truthful words will stand forever, lying speech but a moment.
Lying lips are an abomination to Adonai, but those who deal faithfully are his delight.
Pleasant words are like a honeycomb, sweet to the taste and healing for the body.

Like silver slag overlaid on a clay pot are lips that burn [with friendship] over a hating heart.

He who hates may hide it with his speech; but inside, he harbors deceit.

He may speak pleasantly, but don’t trust him; for seven abominations are in his heart.

His hatred may be concealed by deceit, but his wickedness will be revealed in the assembly.
The tongue of the wise presents knowledge well, but the mouth of a fool spews out folly.
The mind of the righteous thinks before speaking, but the mouth of the wicked spews out evil stuff.
A gossip goes around revealing secrets, but a trustworthy person keeps a confidence.
One can be filled with good as the result of one’s words, and one gets the reward one’s deeds deserve.
Fine speech is unbecoming to a boor, and even less lying lips to a leader.
The north wind brings rain and a backbiting tongue, angry looks.
He who guards his mouth preserves his life, but one who talks too much comes to ruin.
Idle talk can pierce like a sword, but the tongue of the wise can heal.
A gentle response deflects fury, but a harsh word makes tempers rise.
To answer someone before hearing him out is both stupid and embarrassing.
The poor man speaks beseechingly, the rich man’s answer is blunt.
People take pleasure in anything they say; but a word at the right time, how good it is!
Giving an honest answer is like giving a kiss.
Even a fool, if he stays silent, is thought wise; he who keeps his mouth shut can pass for smart.
The tongue has power over life and death; those who indulge it must eat its fruit.
An evildoer heeds wicked lips; a liar listens to destructive talk.
A soothing tongue is a tree of life, but when it twists things, it breaks the spirit.
A knowledgeable person controls his tongue; a discerning person controls his temper.
When words are many, sin is not lacking; so he who controls his speech is wise.
The lips of the righteous feed many, but fools die for lack of sense.
Anxiety in a person’s heart weighs him down, but a kind word cheers him up.
With patience a ruler may be won over, and a gentle tongue can break bones.
Do you see someone too anxious to speak? There is more hope for a fool than for him.
Don’t be a witness against your neighbor for no reason — would you use your lips to deceive?
On the lips of the intelligent is found wisdom, but a stick is in store for the back of a fool.
The words of the wicked are a deadly ambush, but the speech of the upright rescues them.
Wisdom is too lofty for a fool; he keeps his mouth shut at the city gate.
The lips of the wise spread knowledge; not so the hearts of fools.
The tongue of the righteous is like pure silver, but the mind of the wicked is worth little.
Like apples of gold in settings of silver is a word appropriately spoken.
An honest witness will not lie, but a false witness lies with every breath.
Wise people hide their knowledge, but when a fool speaks, ruin is imminent.
A deceitful person stirs up strife, and a slanderer can separate even close friends.
He who belittles another lacks good sense, whereas a person of discernment stays silent.
Whoever greets his neighbor in a loud voice at dawn might just as well have cursed him.
The speech of the righteous is a fountain of life, but the speech of the wicked is a cover for violence.
A cautious person conceals knowledge, but the heart of a fool blurts out folly.
A fool takes no pleasure in trying to understand; he only wants to express his own opinion.
The wicked is trapped by his own sinful speech, but the righteous finds a way out of trouble.
A fool’s anger is known at once, but a cautious person slighted conceals his feelings.
A [good] man enjoys good as a result of what he says, but the essence of the treacherous is violence.
Adonai is far from the wicked, but he listens to the prayer of the righteous.
A crooked-hearted person will find nothing good, and the perverse of speech will end in calamity.
Many ask favors of a generous person — to a giver of gifts, everyone is a friend.
It is a snare to dedicate a gift to God rashly and reflect on the vows only afterwards.
Throw the scoffer out, and quarreling goes too; strife and insults cease.
Like a gold earring, like a fine gold necklace is a wise reprover to a receptive ear.
Like the coldness of snow in the heat of the harvest is a faithful messenger to the one who sends him; he refreshes his master’s spirit.
Like clouds and wind that bring no rain is he who boasts of gifts he never gives.
Like cold water to a person faint from thirst is good news from a distant land.
Like a fluttering sparrow or a flying swallow, an undeserved curse will come home to roost.

Like a madman shooting deadly arrows and firebrands

is one who deceives another, then says, “It was just a joke.”
He who rebukes another person in the end gets more thanks than the flatterer.
A person who flatters his neighbor spreads a net for his own steps.
When a wise man argues with a foolish one, he meets anger and ridicule without relief.
A fool gives vent to all his feelings, but the wise, thinking of afterwards, stills them.
It is not good to be partial to the guilty and thus deprive the innocent of justice.
False scales are an abomination to Adonai, but accurate weights please him.
Adonai detests a double standard in weights, and false scales are not good.
He who tells the truth furthers justice, but a false witness furthers deceit.
To do what is right and just is more pleasing to Adonai than sacrifice.
From under a cloak a bad man takes a bribe to pervert the course of justice.
False weights and false measures — Adonai detests them both.
To show partiality is not good, though a person may do wrong for a crust of bread.
A worthless witness mocks at justice, and the mouth of the wicked swallows wrongdoing.
A false witness will not go unpunished; whoever breathes out lies will not escape.
A truthful witness saves lives, but a liar misdirects [judgment].
A false witness will not go unpunished; whoever breathes out lies will perish.
but with those who condemn him, things will go well, and a good blessing will come upon them.
Evil people don’t understand justice, but those who seek Adonai understand everything.
These also are sayings of the wise: Showing partiality in judgment is not good.
Many seek the ruler’s favor, but it is from Adonai that each gets justice.
The first to state his case seems right, till the other one comes and cross-examines.
He who tells the guilty, “You are innocent,” will be cursed by peoples, reviled by nations;
A lying witness is doomed, but one who heard [what was said] will testify successfully.
To punish the innocent is not right, likewise to flog noble people for their uprightness.
Don’t exploit the helpless, because they are helpless, and don’t crush the poor in court,
He who justifies the wicked and he who condemns the righteous — both alike are an abomination to Adonai.
The greedy for gain brings trouble to his home, but he who hates bribes will live.
The oppressor of the poor insults his maker, but he who is kind to the needy honors him.
A poor man who oppresses the weak is like a downpour that sweeps away all the food.
Both oppressing the poor to enrich oneself and giving to the rich yield only loss.
Don’t move the ancient boundary stone or encroach on the land of the fatherless;
for their Redeemer is strong; he will take up their fight against you.
The eyes of Adonai are everywhere, watching the evil and the good.
Evil will not depart from the house of him who returns evil for good.
He who is kind to the poor is lending to Adonai; and he will repay him for his good deed.
The crooked-hearted are an abomination to Adonai, but those sincere in their ways are his delight.
Depend on it: the evil will not go unpunished; but the offspring of the righteous will escape.
The fields of the poor may yield much food, but some are swept away because of injustice.
He who despises his fellow sins, but he who shows compassion to the humble is happy.
Sh’ol and Abaddon lie open to Adonai; so how much more people’s hearts!
Adonai detests plans to do evil, but kind words are pure.
Adonai made everything for its purpose, even the wicked for the day of disaster.
He who mocks the poor insults his maker; he who rejoices at calamity will not go unpunished.
Casting lots puts an end to strife and separates powerful disputants.
Judgments are in store for scorners and blows for the backs of fools.
Don’t say, “I’ll pay back evil for evil”; wait for Adonai to save you.
The violence of the wicked will sweep them away, because they refuse to act justly.
Whoever stops up his ears at the cry of the poor will himself cry, but not be answered.
He who sows injustice reaps trouble, and the rod of his angry outburst will fail.
for Adonai will plead their case for them and withhold life from those who defraud them.
Don’t move the ancient boundary stone set up by your ancestors.
If you slack off on a day of distress, your strength is small indeed.
Yes, rescue those being dragged off to death — won’t you save those about to be killed?
If you say, “We knew nothing about it,” won’t he who weighs hearts discern it? Yes, he who guards you will know it and repay each one as his deeds deserve.
Don’t rejoice when your enemy falls; don’t let your heart be glad when he stumbles.
For Adonai might see it, and it would displease him; he might withdraw his anger from your foe.
My son, don’t get involved with revolutionaries, but fear Adonai and the king.
For disaster from them will suddenly appear, and who knows what ruin they both can cause?
Don’t say, “I’ll do to him what he did to me, I’ll pay him back what his deeds deserve.”
For it is better to be told, “Come up here,” than be degraded in the presence of a nobleman. What your eyes have seen,
don’t rush to present in a dispute. For what will you do later on, if your neighbor puts you to shame?
Discuss your dispute with your neighbor, but don’t reveal another person’s secrets.
If you do, and he hears of it, he will disgrace you, and your bad reputation will stick.
Like a club, a sword or a sharp arrow is a person who gives false testimony against a neighbor.
Whoever digs a pit will fall into it, and a stone will come back on the one who starts it rolling.
Those who abandon Torah praise the wicked, but those who keep Torah fight them.
Let a man weighed down with anyone’s blood flee to a pit; give him no support.
The accomplice of a thief hates himself; he hears himself put under oath but discloses nothing.
An unjust person is an abomination to the righteous, but he who lives uprightly is an abomination to the wicked.
